title: Selvage Session Protocol — the awareness state and its anchors
description: The state carried inside a `message_type = 1` frame, which y-protocols leaves opaque: `{ path, selection }`, and each selection endpoint a yjs `RelativePosition` anchor. Valid against PROTOCOL.md §8.1. A binary frame is relayed unchanged and is not canonicalised (CANONICAL.md §6), so nothing here says how a state is written, only what a receiver may read.

anchorItem.description: The element a position sits against: a CRDT item, named by the client that made it and the clock of the change. When it is present it is authoritative for the position, and a scope beside it is a check on the element rather than a second way of naming the position (§8.1).

client.description: The CRDT client id that created the item. This is a y-protocols number inside the payload, not the session's `awareness_client_id`.

clock.description: The item's clock in that client's sequence. The CRDT clock is unaffected by the offset unit an adapter chooses (§8.1).

anchor.description: A yjs `RelativePosition`: a scope, an optional element, and an association. At least one of `item`/`tname`/`type` is present, and at most one scope. A receiver resolves it against the `Y.Text` named by the state's `path`, and a state whose endpoint does not resolve carries no selection rather than a guessed position (§8.1).

assoc.description: `0` for the element after the position, `-1` for the one before. Omitted means `0`. A receiver normalises any other number by sign, and any number is an `assoc` whatever its precision (§8.1; `NOTES.md` §B.4).

tname.description: A root type name, which for Selvage is the document path. `tname` with no `item` denotes an end of that text, chosen by `assoc`: the end when `assoc >= 0`, the start when it is negative.

type.description: A nested type name. This protocol produces none, so a scope resolving anywhere other than the `Y.Text` for `path` fails to resolve.

selection.description: The two endpoints an editor selection has. `head` resolving before `anchor` means the selection was made backwards: direction stays implicit in which endpoint lands further left, and a caret is two endpoints that resolve to the same index (§8.1).

state.description: One awareness state, keyed on the wire by the client id that published it. A state with `path` and no `selection` says only which document the peer is in — the encoding for a selection the sender could not anchor (§8.1). Identity is not here: a display name travels in the session layer (§8.4).

path.description: The document the state is about. It normally names a path in the room's open-document set; a state naming another path is still relayed and may still be displayed, because the set is shared and is not the sender's to guarantee (§8.1).
